title: Act on the Prevention of Insolvency and Structural Improvement of Fisheries Cooperatives
title_original: 수산업협동조합의 부실예방 및 구조개선에 관한 법률
full_text:
Chapter I General Provisions <Amended on March 17, 2010>

Article 1 (Purpose) The purpose of this Act is to protect cooperative members, depositors, and other persons and contribute to the sound development of cooperatives by prescribing matters concerning the prevention of insolvency of cooperatives established under the Fisheries Cooperatives Act and their structural improvement, including mergers and the disposal of non-performing assets. <Amended on February 18, 2020>

Article 2 (Definitions) The terms used in this Act have the following meanings. <Amended on March 23, 2013 and February 18, 2020>
1. The term “cooperative” means a district fisheries cooperative, a fisheries cooperative organized by business category, or a fishery products processing fisheries cooperative established under the Fisheries Cooperatives Act (hereinafter referred to as the “Fisheries Cooperatives Act”).
2. The term “Federation” means the National Federation of Fisheries Cooperatives established under the Fisheries Cooperatives Act.
3. The term “insolvent cooperative” means a cooperative falling under any of the following subparagraphs and designated under Article 4:
a. A cooperative whose liabilities exceed its assets according to an assessment of its management condition, or a cooperative for which it is clear that normal management will be difficult because of a financial incident involving a large amount of money or the occurrence of non-performing claims. In such cases, methods for assessing management condition and standards for the valuation and calculation of liabilities and assets shall be prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries.
b. A cooperative that has suspended payment of claims on deposits, etc. or repayment of borrowings from the State, public bodies, the Federation, or other financial institutions.
c. A cooperative that has difficulty paying claims on deposits, etc. or repaying borrowings without external financial assistance or borrowings.
4. The term “cooperative at risk of insolvency” means a cooperative designated under Article 4 whose financial condition falls below the standards prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries and which is therefore highly likely to become an insolvent cooperative.
5. The term “business” means business under Articles 60, 107, and 112 of the Fisheries Cooperatives Act and Articles 9 and 10 of the Addenda to Act No. 7311, the Act Amending the Fisheries Cooperatives Act.
6. The term “deposits, etc.” means any of the following. However, funds received from persons prescribed by Presidential Decree, including the Government and local governments, may be excluded:
a. Deposits and installment savings received by a cooperative through its credit business.
b. Mutual aid contributions received by cooperatives and the Federation through their mutual aid business.
7. The term “depositors, etc.” means persons holding claims on deposits, etc. against a cooperative or the Federation.
8. The term “claims on deposits, etc.” means any of the following:
a. Claims held by depositors, etc. against a cooperative for the principal and interest of deposits and installment savings or other agreed sums of money.
b. Claims held by depositors, etc. against cooperatives and the Federation for mutual aid benefits or other agreed sums of money under mutual aid contracts.
9. The term “insured event” means any of the following:
a. Suspension of payment of claims on deposits, etc. (hereinafter referred to as a “type 1 insured event”).
b. Revocation of a cooperative's establishment authorization, a resolution to dissolve a cooperative, or a declaration of bankruptcy (hereinafter referred to as a “type 2 insured event”).
10. The term “financial assistance” means any of the following assistance provided by the management agency at the expense of the Fund to an insolvent cooperative or a cooperative at risk of insolvency (hereinafter referred to as “insolvent cooperatives, etc.”), or to a person intending to take over an insolvent cooperative, etc. or acquire its business under Article 6, for purposes including improvement of the financial structure of the insolvent cooperative, etc.:
a. A contribution or the purchase of assets.
b. A guarantee or assumption of liabilities.
c. A loan of funds.
11. The term “Fund” means the Mutual Finance Depositor Protection Fund established and operated within the Federation under Article 20.
12. The term “management agency” means the Federation that manages the Fund under Article 22.
13. The term “Fund Management Committee” means the committee established within the management agency under Article 21 to deliberate and decide on matters concerning the operation of the Fund.

Article 3 (Responsibilities of the Federation)
① The Federation shall develop and improve systems to prevent the insolvency of cooperatives.
② To facilitate the prevention of insolvency of cooperatives and related activities and manage them efficiently, the Federation may establish a computerized insolvency prevention system.

Chapter I-2 Prevention of Insolvency of Cooperatives <Newly inserted on February 18, 2020>

Article 3-2 (Management Risk Assessment)
① To prevent the insolvency of cooperatives, the Federation shall conduct a monthly management risk assessment of cooperatives that are not insolvent cooperatives, etc. (hereinafter referred to as “normal cooperatives” in this Chapter).
② Taking into account the results of the management risk assessment under paragraph ①, the Federation shall determine the management risk ratings of normal cooperatives in accordance with standards prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries.
③ The Federation shall notify normal cooperatives of the results of the management risk assessment under paragraph ① and the ratings determined under paragraph ② and report them to the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries.
④ Matters necessary for the standards, procedures, and methods for the management risk assessment under paragraph ① and the procedures and methods for notification and reporting under paragraph ③ shall be prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries.

Article 3-3 (Designation of Cooperatives Subject to Management Supervision)
① The Minister of Oceans and Fisheries may designate a normal cooperative as a cooperative subject to management supervision if it falls under any of the following:
1. Its rating determined under Article 3-2, paragraph ②, meets the criteria prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries.
2. It is otherwise recognized, on the basis of the management risk assessment under Article 3-2, paragraph ①, that management risks are increasing rapidly because of a decline in its net capital ratio, a financial incident, the occurrence of non-performing claims, or similar circumstances.
② If the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries designates a cooperative subject to management supervision under paragraph ①, the Minister shall notify the cooperative concerned and the Federation of that fact.

Article 3-4 (Management of Cooperatives Subject to Management Supervision)
① The Minister of Oceans and Fisheries may require a cooperative designated under Article 3-3, paragraph ① (hereinafter referred to as a “cooperative subject to management supervision”) to submit a management improvement plan and may require revisions or additions if the submitted plan is considered insufficient.
② Among cooperatives subject to management supervision, the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries may require those meeting the criteria prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries, including cooperatives at risk of being designated as insolvent cooperatives, etc., to take all or some of the following corrective actions. In such cases, the Minister may require the cooperative concerned to submit an action plan addressing the corrective measures required:
1. Formulation of a cost reduction plan.
2. Re-examination of the viability of new businesses and new capital investments.
3. Establishment of special allowances for bad debts.
4. Formulation of measures to improve the standards for handling lending and deposit-taking and the applicable interest rates.
5. Formulation of measures to improve fund management.
6. Re-examination of the viability of fixed asset investment projects.
7. Formulation of a plan to maintain an appropriate level of inventories.
8. Formulation of a plan to increase equity capital.
9. Other measures comparable to those in items 1 through 8 that are considered necessary to prevent insolvency.
③ The Minister of Oceans and Fisheries may inspect quarterly the implementation of corrective measures by a cooperative required to take such measures under paragraph ②.
④ If a cooperative required to take corrective measures under paragraph ② falls under any of the following, the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries shall notify that cooperative of the termination of the corrective requirements:
1. It has implemented all corrective measures required under paragraph ②.
2. It is recognized that implementation of the corrective measures required under paragraph ② is no longer necessary because of improvements in fund management or similar circumstances.
3. Its designation as a cooperative subject to management supervision has been lifted under Article 3-5, paragraph ②.
⑤ In addition to matters provided for in paragraphs ① through ④, matters necessary for the submission of management improvement plans, procedures for requiring corrective measures, submission of action plans, termination of corrective requirements, and related matters shall be prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries.

Article 3-5 (Lifting the Designation of Cooperatives Subject to Management Supervision)
① When six months have elapsed since a cooperative was designated as a cooperative subject to management supervision, the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries shall review whether it no longer falls under any of the items of Article 3-3, paragraph ①, taking into account the reports under Article 3-2, paragraph ③.
② If the review under paragraph ① shows that it is no longer necessary to manage the cooperative as a cooperative subject to management supervision, the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries shall lift its designation.
③ If the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries lifts a designation under paragraph ②, the Minister shall notify the cooperative concerned and the Federation of that fact.

Chapter II Management and Support of Insolvent Cooperatives, etc.

Article 4 (Designation of Insolvent Cooperatives, etc.)
① For a cooperative falling under any of the subparagraphs of Article 2, item 3, or a cooperative highly likely to become insolvent under item 4 of that Article, the management agency shall, following a resolution of the Fund Management Committee, request the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries to designate it as an insolvent cooperative, etc. However, a resolution of the Fund Management Committee shall not be required for a cooperative falling under Article 2, item 3 b.
② If the management agency makes a request under paragraph ① and the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries considers it necessary to manage the cooperative as an insolvent cooperative, etc., the Minister shall designate it accordingly and notify the cooperative concerned and the management agency of that fact.

Article 4-2 (Prompt Corrective Action)
① The Minister of Oceans and Fisheries shall recommend, require, or order the following measures (hereinafter referred to as “prompt corrective action”) with respect to insolvent cooperatives, etc. or their officers and, if the Minister issues an order, shall order the submission of an implementation plan. In such cases, the Minister shall notify the management agency of matters including the prompt corrective action recommended, required, or ordered. <Amended on March 23, 2013 and February 18, 2020>
1. A caution or warning to the cooperative, and a caution, warning, reprimand, or salary reduction for its officers and employees.
2. Reduction of paid-in capital, increase of equity capital, disposal of assets held, or reduction of branches or the organizational structure.
3. Prohibition on the acquisition of risky assets or restriction on deposit-taking at abnormally high interest rates.
4. Suspension of officers from their duties or appointment of an administrator to perform their duties on their behalf.
5. Suspension of all or part of the business (hereinafter referred to as “suspension of business”).
6. Merger.
7. Transfer of all or part of the business (hereinafter referred to as a “business transfer”) or transfer of contracts relating to all or part of the business (hereinafter referred to as a “contract transfer”).
8. Other measures comparable to those in items 1 through 7 that are considered necessary to improve the financial soundness of the cooperative.
② When recommending, requiring, or ordering prompt corrective action, the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries shall recommend or require such action with respect to a cooperative at risk of insolvency or its officers according to the degree of that risk, and shall order such action with respect to an insolvent cooperative or its officers. The Minister shall determine and publicly announce in advance the standards and content necessary for prompt corrective action. <Amended on February 18, 2020>
③ If the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries determines that an insolvent cooperative, etc. temporarily falling short of the standards under the latter sentence of paragraph ② can meet those standards within a short period, or recognizes comparable grounds, the Minister may defer prompt corrective action for a specified period. <Amended on March 23, 2013 and February 18, 2020>
④ When establishing the standards under the latter sentence of paragraph ②, provision shall be made so that orders for the complete suspension of business, transfer of the entire business, transfer of all contracts, and comparable measures that may cause substantial property losses to an insolvent cooperative, etc. or its members may be issued only if the cooperative is an insolvent cooperative, or its financial condition falls substantially short of the standards under the latter sentence of paragraph ② and it is recognized that there is a manifest risk of harm to sound credit order or to the rights and interests of depositors, etc. <Amended on February 18, 2020>
⑤ When an insolvent cooperative, etc. resolves on a merger under paragraph ①, item 6, the resolution may be adopted with the attendance or votes of a majority of all members and the approval of a majority of the members attending or voting, notwithstanding the proviso to Article 40 and Article 43, paragraph 2, of the Fisheries Cooperatives Act (including cases where those provisions apply mutatis mutandis under Article 108 or 113 of that Act). The same shall apply when a cooperative merging with an insolvent cooperative, etc. resolves on the merger. <Amended on February 18, 2020>
⑥ Paragraph ⑤ shall apply mutatis mutandis when a cooperative resolves on a business transfer or contract transfer under paragraph ①, item 7, or intends to acquire a business or receive a contract transfer. For a cooperative with delegates, “members” shall be construed as “delegates” and “members voting” as “delegates voting.”
⑦ If a cooperative intends, under paragraphs ⑤ and ⑥, to hold a resolution of its general meeting or delegates' meeting, a members' vote, or a similar procedure concerning a merger, business transfer, or contract transfer, the management agency shall notify the cooperative's members or delegates in advance of matters relevant to the resolution or vote, including the degree of the cooperative's insolvency and measures concerning the merger, business transfer, or contract transfer.

Article 4-3 (Changes to Prompt Corrective Action, etc.) If an insolvent cooperative, etc. falls under any of the following, the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries may change the prompt corrective action and recommend, require, or order the action as changed. In such cases, the Minister may, if necessary, hear the opinion of the management agency and require it to investigate the management condition of the cooperative concerned or take measures prescribed by Presidential Decree, including a management diagnosis.
1. It has not completed the prompt corrective action recommended, required, or ordered within the prescribed period.
2. It is considered difficult for it to complete the prompt corrective action recommended, required, or ordered.

Article 5 (Support Measures for Implementing Prompt Corrective Action, etc.)
① When recommending, requiring, or ordering a merger, business transfer, or contract transfer under Article 4-2, paragraph ①, the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries may designate another cooperative and recommend that it merge with the cooperative subject to the recommendation, requirement, or order, acquire its business, or receive the contract transfer. <Amended on March 23, 2013 and February 18, 2020>
② The management agency may present the amount, conditions, and other terms of financial assistance to a cooperative recommended under paragraph ① to merge, acquire a business, or receive a contract transfer, on condition that it implements that recommendation.

Article 6 (Application for Financial Assistance) A person intending to take over an insolvent cooperative, etc. through a contract transfer or merger, or to acquire its business, may apply to the management agency for financial assistance.

Article 7 (Financial Assistance)
① The management agency may provide financial assistance in accordance with a resolution of the Fund Management Committee in any of the following cases:
1. It receives an application for financial assistance under Article 6.
2. Assistance is considered necessary to facilitate the merger, business transfer, or contract transfer of an insolvent cooperative, etc.
3. Improvement of the financial structure of an insolvent cooperative, etc. is considered necessary to protect depositors, etc. and stabilize credit order.
② Matters necessary for the standards, methods, conditions, and other aspects of financial assistance under paragraph ① shall be determined by the management agency following a resolution of the Fund Management Committee. <Amended on February 18, 2020>

Article 8 (Principles of Financial Assistance)
① When providing financial assistance, the management agency shall do so on condition that persons responsible for the insolvency of the recipient cooperative bear a fair share of the losses.
② The management agency shall provide financial assistance on condition that the recipient cooperative makes its own efforts toward structural improvement, and may divide the assistance into two or more installments.
③ Deleted. <February 18, 2020>

Article 9 (Conclusion of an Implementation Agreement for Management Normalization, etc.)
① To provide financial assistance to a cooperative, the management agency shall conclude an implementation agreement for management normalization (hereinafter referred to as an “agreement”) with that cooperative. However, for a cooperative that is not an insolvent cooperative, etc., the management agency may refrain from concluding an agreement on matters other than those specified in paragraph ②, item 3. <Amended on February 18, 2020>
② The agreement shall contain the following matters for the normalization of the management of the cooperative concerned:
1. Target levels for financial soundness standards prescribed by Presidential Decree, including the net capital ratio.
2. Target levels for profitability standards prescribed by Presidential Decree, including return on assets.
3. Matters concerning the stable management of the funds provided, including deposits with the Federation, and the plan for their repayment.
4. Other matters prescribed by Presidential Decree as necessary for normalization of the cooperative's management.
③ The management agency shall disclose the content of the agreement through electronic media or other means. However, this shall not apply to matters prescribed by Presidential Decree whose content may have a significant effect on the management of the cooperative concerned.
④ When requested by the competent standing committee of the National Assembly, the management agency shall report the results of implementation of the agreement.
⑤ Deleted. <February 18, 2020>

Article 9-2 (Management of Cooperatives That Have Concluded Agreements)
① For a cooperative that has concluded an agreement under Article 9, paragraph ①, the management agency shall inspect the results of implementation of the agreement and the progress of management improvement, up to twice per year.
② If an inspection under paragraph ① shows a risk of further deterioration in the cooperative's financial structure or insufficient improvement in that structure, the management agency may provide necessary support, including management guidance.
③ If a cooperative falls under any of the following, the management agency may require the chairperson of the cooperative to remedy the situation, or require the dismissal or suspension from duties of its officers or disciplinary action against its employees:
1. It has failed to implement the agreement.
2. It has prepared false reports or materials required under Article 9 or the agreement, or neglected to submit them without justifiable grounds.
④ The management agency shall report the results of inspections and support under paragraphs ① and ② to the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries.

Article 9-3 (Lifting the Designation of Insolvent Cooperatives, etc.)
① If the management agency recognizes that an insolvent cooperative, etc. does not fall under any of the subparagraphs of Article 2, item 3, and is not a cooperative highly likely to become insolvent under item 4 of that Article, it shall, following a resolution of the Fund Management Committee, request the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries to lift its designation as an insolvent cooperative, etc. or change the designation of an insolvent cooperative to that of a cooperative at risk of insolvency. In such cases, the management agency may also request the termination or modification of the prompt corrective action recommended, required, or ordered for the cooperative.
② Upon a request from the management agency under the former sentence of paragraph ①, the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries shall lift the designation or change it to that of a cooperative at risk of insolvency according to the following categories, and notify the cooperative concerned and the management agency of that fact. In such cases, the Minister shall also notify them whether the prompt corrective action recommended, required, or ordered will be terminated or modified in response to the management agency's request under the latter sentence of paragraph ①:
1. If it is recognized that the cooperative no longer needs to be managed as an insolvent cooperative, etc.: the designation as an insolvent cooperative, etc. shall be lifted.
2. If it is recognized that an insolvent cooperative needs to be managed under a changed designation as a cooperative at risk of insolvency: the designation shall be changed to that of a cooperative at risk of insolvency.

Article 10 (Administrative Dispositions)
① If an insolvent cooperative, etc. violates or fails to comply with a requirement or order under Article 4-2, paragraph ①, the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries may, after hearing the opinion of the Fund Management Committee, order the suspension of the cooperative's officers from their duties and appoint an administrator to perform their duties on their behalf, or recommend their dismissal to the general meeting (meaning the delegates' meeting in the case of officers elected by that meeting or a cooperative chairperson elected by the board of directors). In such cases, notwithstanding Article 57, paragraph 2, of the Fisheries Cooperatives Act (including cases where it applies mutatis mutandis under Article 108 or 113 of that Act), the resolution shall be adopted with the attendance of a majority of all members or delegates and the approval of a majority of those members or delegates attending. <Amended on March 23, 2013 and February 18, 2020>
② If an insolvent cooperative falls under any of the following, the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries may, after hearing the opinion of the Fund Management Committee, take necessary dispositions against it, including a decision on a contract transfer, suspension of business for a specified period not exceeding six months, or revocation of its establishment authorization. However, in the case of item 1, if the reason for failure to comply with the order is the result of a resolution of the general meeting or delegates' meeting or a members' vote under Article 4-2, paragraphs ⑤ and ⑥, the Minister shall give the cooperative an opportunity to explain its position before taking a disposition, as prescribed by Presidential Decree. <Amended on March 23, 2013 and February 18, 2020>
1. It fails to comply with an order under Article 4-2, paragraph ①, or has become unable to comply with it.
2. Its liabilities far exceed its assets, making compliance with an order under Article 4-2, paragraph ①, appear difficult.
3. Its funding situation has deteriorated rapidly, making payment of claims on deposits, etc. or repayment of borrowings difficult, and it is recognized as clear that the rights and interests of depositors, etc. or credit order will be harmed.
③ Before revoking an establishment authorization under paragraph ②, the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries shall hold a hearing. <Amended on March 23, 2013>
④ When deciding on a contract transfer under paragraph ②, the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries shall determine, to the extent necessary, the scope and conditions of the contracts to be transferred and the cooperative to receive them (hereinafter referred to as the “acquiring cooperative”), and obtain its consent in advance. In such cases, the management agency may submit its opinion to the Minister on the detailed procedures concerning the scope and conditions of the contracts to be transferred and the consent of the acquiring cooperative. <Amended on March 23, 2013 and February 18, 2020>
⑤ The Minister of Oceans and Fisheries shall appoint an administrator under paragraph ① for a cooperative ordered to transfer contracts under paragraph ②. <Amended on March 23, 2013>
⑥ Article 4-2, paragraph ⑤, shall apply mutatis mutandis when an acquiring cooperative under paragraph ④ intends to consent to matters concerning a contract transfer. For a cooperative with delegates, “members” shall be construed as “delegates.” <Amended on February 18, 2020>
⑦ A decision on a contract transfer under paragraph ② shall not require a resolution of the general meeting (meaning the delegates' meeting for a cooperative operating such a meeting), notwithstanding Article 4-2, paragraph ⑥, the Fisheries Cooperatives Act, and the articles of association of the insolvent cooperative concerned. <Amended on February 18, 2020>

Article 11 (Effect of a Decision on a Contract Transfer)
① If a contract transfer is decided under Article 10, paragraph ②, the acquiring cooperative shall succeed, at the time of that decision, to the rights and obligations of the insolvent cooperative under contracts relating to the business covered by the decision.
② If a contract transfer is decided under Article 10, paragraph ②, the insolvent cooperative concerned and the acquiring cooperative shall jointly and without delay publicly announce the substance of the decision and the fact of the contract transfer in at least two daily newspapers.
③ Upon the public announcement under paragraph ②, the acquiring cooperative shall succeed, on the same terms, to the legal relationships between the insolvent cooperative concerned and the creditors, debtors, third-party providers of collateral, and other interested parties relating to the contract transfer (hereinafter referred to as “interested parties”). In such cases, interested parties may assert against the acquiring cooperative grounds arising in their relationships with the insolvent cooperative before the public announcement under paragraph ②.
④ Upon the public announcement under paragraph ②, the announcement shall be deemed to satisfy the requirements for asserting an assignment of nominative claims against third parties under Article 450 of the Civil Act. In such cases, interested parties may assert against the acquiring cooperative grounds arising in their relationships with the insolvent cooperative before the announcement.
⑤ If a contract transfer is decided under Article 10, paragraph ②, the acquiring cooperative shall acquire rights relating to real estate and other property whose transfer requires registration or recordation at the time of the public announcement under paragraph ②.
⑥ When a contract transfer is decided under Article 10, paragraph ②, the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries shall require the insolvent cooperative concerned and the acquiring cooperative to retain and manage materials relating to the transfer and make them available for inspection by interested parties. In such cases, the standards and procedures necessary for retention, management, and inspection shall be prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries. <Amended on March 23, 2013 and February 18, 2020>

Article 12 (Appointment and Duties of Administrators, etc.)
① An administrator appointed under Article 4-2, paragraph ①, item 4, or Article 10, paragraphs ① and ⑤, shall, according to the purpose of the appointment, have the authority to perform the duties of the officer concerned or to manage and dispose of the assets, liabilities, and other matters of the insolvent cooperative within the scope of work relating to the decision on a contract transfer. <Amended on February 18, 2020>
② If the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries orders the complete suspension of a cooperative's business or decides on a contract transfer under Article 4-2, paragraph ①, item 5, or Article 10, paragraph ② (excluding a case in which complete suspension is ordered because of a temporary shortage of funds and management normalization is considered certain), the Minister may appoint an officer or employee of the Federation as administrator, as prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries. However, if necessary for the normalization of the cooperative's management or the protection of general creditors, the Minister may appoint a person other than an officer or employee of the Federation as administrator. <Amended on March 23, 2013 and February 18, 2020>
③ The Minister of Oceans and Fisheries may issue orders necessary for the performance of duties to an administrator under paragraph ①. <Amended on March 23, 2013>
④ If considered necessary for the smooth implementation of prompt corrective action, the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries may dismiss an administrator under paragraph ①. <Amended on March 23, 2013>
⑤ Upon appointing an administrator under paragraph ①, the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries shall, without delay, notify the district court having jurisdiction over the location of the cooperative's principal office and commission the registry office having jurisdiction over that location to register the administrator's appointment. <Amended on March 23, 2013 and September 20, 2024>
⑥ Article 11, paragraph 1, of the Commercial Act and Articles 30 and 360 through 362 of the Debtor Rehabilitation and Bankruptcy Act shall apply mutatis mutandis to administrators. In such cases, “manager” in the Commercial Act shall be construed as “administrator,” and “bankruptcy trustee” and “court” in the Debtor Rehabilitation and Bankruptcy Act shall be construed as “administrator” and “Minister of Oceans and Fisheries,” respectively. <Amended on March 23, 2013>

Article 13 (Purchase of Claims on Deposits, etc.)
① When the management agency has paid insurance proceeds or paid part of the claims on deposits, etc. in advance under Article 30, paragraphs ① and ②, it may, at the request of depositors, etc., purchase claims on deposits, etc. relating to the insured event concerned, excluding rights acquired by the management agency under Article 33.
② When purchasing claims on deposits, etc. under paragraph ①, the management agency shall pay depositors, etc. an estimated amount of the value of those claims. If the amount recovered on the claims purchased by the management agency, less the expenses incurred, exceeds the amount paid to depositors, etc., the agency shall make an additional payment of that excess to the depositors, etc. concerned.
③ In addition to matters provided for in paragraphs ① and ②, matters necessary for the purchase of claims on deposits, etc. shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 13-2 (Measures for Inability to Pay Deposits, etc.) If there is a risk of substantial harm to the interests of members and depositors, etc., including a risk of bankruptcy of a cooperative or inability to pay deposits, etc., and the management agency so requests, the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries may order restrictions on the acceptance of deposits, etc. and on lending, suspension of payment of all or part of the claims on deposits, etc., or other necessary measures.

Article 14 (Petition for Bankruptcy) If the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries becomes aware that facts constituting grounds for bankruptcy under Article 306 of the Debtor Rehabilitation and Bankruptcy Act exist in respect of a cooperative, the Minister may file a petition for bankruptcy, notwithstanding Article 85 of the Fisheries Cooperatives Act. <Amended on March 23, 2013>

Article 15 (Liquidator or Bankruptcy Trustee)
① If a cooperative is dissolved and the management agency is its largest creditor as prescribed by Presidential Decree, a person appointed by the management agency from among the Federation's officers and employees, following a resolution of the Fund Management Committee, shall become the liquidator, notwithstanding Article 86 of the Fisheries Cooperatives Act.
② If a cooperative becomes bankrupt and the court appoints a bankruptcy trustee under Article 355 of the Debtor Rehabilitation and Bankruptcy Act, the management agency may, following a resolution of the Fund Management Committee, recommend one of the Federation's officers or employees as bankruptcy trustee.
③ Articles 17 through 23 of the Act on the Structural Improvement of the Financial Industry shall apply mutatis mutandis to the bankruptcy of a cooperative. In such cases, “financial institution” shall be construed as “cooperative,” and “institution participating in bankruptcy” as “management agency.”

Article 16 (Management Agency's Right of Subrogated Setoff) The management agency may, on behalf of depositors, etc., set off each depositor's claims on deposits, etc. existing as of the date of the public announcement of the commencement of insurance benefit payments and other matters under Article 30, paragraph ③ (hereinafter referred to as the “insurance payment announcement date”), against the debts that the depositor owes to the cooperative concerned. Claims on deposits, etc. provided by depositors, etc. to the cooperative as collateral for another person shall be excluded, and guarantee obligations shall be excluded from the debts to be set off.

Article 17 (Requirement to Take Out Liability Insurance, etc.)
① The management agency may require a cooperative (limited to cooperatives meeting criteria prescribed by Presidential Decree, including impairment of equity capital) to take out insurance to compensate for property losses suffered by the cooperative as a result of defaults or tortious acts of its officers and employees. Insurance includes mutual aid coverage under the Fisheries Cooperatives Act and is hereinafter referred to as “insurance” in this Article.
② If a cooperative fails to comply with the requirement to take out insurance under paragraph ①, the management agency may conclude an insurance contract on behalf of that cooperative.
③ If a cooperative does not bear the premiums and other expenses of an insurance contract concluded under paragraph ②, the management agency may deduct them from premiums paid by that cooperative under Article 29, paragraph ①. In such cases, the corresponding amount shall be deemed not to have been paid as premiums.
④ Matters necessary for the methods, procedures, and other aspects of requiring insurance coverage or acting on behalf of a cooperative under paragraph ① or ② shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 18 (Requirement to Exercise Claims for Damages, etc.)
① In any of the following cases, the management agency may require the insolvent cooperative, etc. concerned to claim damages from officers or employees, persons falling under any of the items of Article 401-2, paragraph 1, of the Commercial Act, or other third parties considered responsible for its insolvency or risk of insolvency (hereinafter referred to as “persons responsible for insolvency”):
1. Financial assistance has been decided or provided under Article 7.
2. Insurance proceeds have been paid or part of the claims on deposits, etc. have been paid in advance under Article 30, paragraphs ① and ②.
② A requirement made by the management agency under paragraph ① shall be in writing, stating its grounds, the method of claiming damages, and the period for making the claim.
③ If an insolvent cooperative, etc. fails to comply with a requirement under paragraph ①, the management agency may immediately claim damages by subrogation to that cooperative.
④ If an insolvent cooperative, etc. pursues a damages claim under paragraph ① through litigation, the management agency may intervene in the pending proceedings to assist that cooperative. In such cases, Articles 71 through 77 of the Civil Procedure Act shall apply mutatis mutandis.
⑤ If the management agency prevails after exercising a claim for damages by subrogation under paragraph ③ or intervenes in litigation under paragraph ④ at the request of an insolvent cooperative, etc., that cooperative shall bear the costs.
⑥ If an insolvent cooperative, etc. becomes bankrupt, a claim for costs not paid under paragraph ⑤ shall be deemed an estate claim.
⑦ If necessary for requiring a damages claim, exercising a claim for damages by subrogation, or intervening in litigation under paragraphs ① through ④, the management agency may investigate the business and property condition of the corporation in liquidation or bankruptcy estate of the insolvent cooperative, etc. concerned. <Amended on February 18, 2020>
⑧ Paragraphs ① through ⑥ shall apply mutatis mutandis to a cooperative surviving a merger with an insolvent cooperative, etc. In such cases, the management agency may request that cooperative to submit materials necessary for a claim for damages against persons responsible for insolvency or for intervention in litigation, and the cooperative receiving the request shall comply unless there are special grounds for not doing so.

Article 19 (Request for Provision of Materials) If necessary for the management agency to claim damages from persons responsible for insolvency or intervene in litigation, the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries may request the heads of relevant central administrative agencies, local governments, or other public institutions prescribed by Presidential Decree (hereinafter referred to as “public institutions”) to provide materials or information concerning the property of persons responsible for insolvency. The head of a public institution receiving such a request shall comply unless there are special grounds for not doing so. <Amended on March 23, 2013>

Chapter III Mutual Finance Depositor Protection Fund

Section 1 Establishment of the Mutual Finance Depositor Protection Fund and the Fund Management Committee

Article 20 (Establishment and Financial Resources of the Fund)
① A Mutual Finance Depositor Protection Fund shall be established and operated within the Federation to address situations in which a cooperative engaging in credit or mutual aid business (including the Federation for mutual aid business; the same shall apply hereinafter) is unable to pay claims on deposits, etc. because of bankruptcy or other grounds, and to promote the sound development of cooperatives.
② The Fund shall be formed from the following resources. <Amended on May 29, 2016>
1. Insurance premiums paid by cooperatives.
2. Contributions from the Government.
3. Contributions from the Federation.
4. Borrowings from the Government, the Bank of Korea under the Bank of Korea Act, the Federation, Suhyup Bank established under the Fisheries Cooperatives Act, or financial institutions.
5. Funds recovered from financial assistance provided to insolvent cooperatives, etc. under Article 7.
6. Funds recovered on claims on deposits, etc. purchased or acquired by the management agency under Article 13, paragraph ①, and Article 33.
7. Funds raised through the issuance of Mutual Finance Depositor Protection Fund bonds (hereinafter referred to as “Fund bonds”) under Article 27, paragraph ②.
8. Income from the operation of the Fund and other receipts.

Article 21 (Fund Management Committee)
① The management agency shall establish a Fund Management Committee to deliberate and decide on the following matters concerning the operation of the Fund. <Amended on March 23, 2013 and February 18, 2020>
1. Formation, operation, and management of the Fund.
2. Establishment of the target size of the Fund's reserves under Article 29-2, payment of insurance proceeds, and related matters.
3. Designation of insolvent cooperatives, etc., lifting of such designations, support for such cooperatives, and related matters.
4. Borrowing of funds.
5. Issuance of Fund bonds.
6. Enactment, amendment, and repeal of regulations relating to the Fund.
7. Other matters submitted to a meeting at the request of the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries or because the Fund Management Committee considers them necessary.
② The Fund Management Committee shall consist of the following members, including one chairperson and one vice-chairperson. The chairperson shall be the chairperson of the Federation, and the vice-chairperson shall be the chairperson of the Cooperative Audit Committee under Article 143 of the Fisheries Cooperatives Act. <Amended on March 23, 2013 and October 1, 2025>
1. One person commissioned by the chairperson of the Federation from among the chairpersons of cooperatives. However, chairpersons of insolvent cooperatives or cooperatives at risk of insolvency shall be excluded.
2. One person designated by the chairperson of the Federation from among its officers and employees.
3. One person designated by the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries from among public officials belonging to the Ministry.
4. One person designated by the Minister of Finance and Economy from among public officials belonging to the Ministry.
4-2. One person designated by the Minister of Planning and Budget from among public officials belonging to the Ministry.
5. One person designated by the chairperson of the Financial Services Commission from among public officials belonging to the Commission.
6. Two persons with extensive knowledge and experience concerning fisheries and cooperatives, commissioned by a fisheries-related organization designated by the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries (limited to a nonprofit corporation established under Article 32 of the Civil Act).
7. Two persons with extensive knowledge and experience concerning cooperatives, finance, and accounting, commissioned by the competent standing committee of the National Assembly.
8. One person with extensive knowledge and experience concerning finance and accounting, commissioned by the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries.
③ The term of office of members under paragraph ②, item 1 and items 6 through 8, shall be three years, and they may be reappointed.
④ In addition to matters provided for in paragraphs ① through ③, matters necessary for the operation of the Fund Management Committee shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Section 2 Management and Operation

Article 22 (Management Agency)
① The Federation shall be the management agency of the Fund.
② When requested by the competent standing committee of the National Assembly, the management agency shall submit a report on the operation of the Fund and related matters.

Article 23 (Duties of the Management Agency) The management agency shall perform the following duties to achieve the purposes of this Act:
1. Requiring the exercise of claims for damages and taking other measures under Article 18.
2. Collecting insurance premiums under Article 29.
3. Paying insurance proceeds and making other payments under Article 30.
4. Duties entrusted or assigned by the Government for the protection of depositors, etc.
5. Duties incidental to those under items 1 through 4.
6. Other duties concerning the management and support of insolvent cooperatives, etc. under this Act.

Article 24 (Uses of the Fund) The Fund may be used only for the following purposes. <Amended on February 18, 2020>
1. Financial assistance under Article 7.
2. Purchase of claims on deposits, etc. under Article 13, paragraph ①.
3. Repayment of principal and interest on borrowings and Fund bonds under Article 20, paragraph ②, items 4 and 7.
4. Payment of insurance proceeds and other payments under Article 30, paragraphs ① and ②.
5. Other expenses necessary for the operation and management of the Fund.

Article 25 (Surplus Funds) The management agency may invest surplus funds of the Fund in the following ways:
1. Purchase of government bonds, public bonds, or other securities designated by the Fund Management Committee.
2. Deposits with, or short-term loans to, financial institutions designated by the Fund Management Committee.
3. Other methods determined by the Fund Management Committee.

Section 3 Finance and Accounting

Article 26 (Accounting of the Fund)
① The fiscal year of the Fund shall be the same as that of the Government.
② The budget and settlement of accounts of the Fund shall be approved by the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries following a resolution of the Fund Management Committee. <Amended on March 23, 2013>
③ The accounts of the Fund and the Federation shall be kept separately, and the Fund shall maintain separate accounts for the credit business sector and the mutual aid business sector.
④ The Fund Management Committee shall determine matters necessary for loans, fund transfers, calculation of expenses, and other transactions between the accounts under paragraph ③.

Article 27 (Borrowing of Funds and Issuance of Fund Bonds)
① The Government may guarantee repayment of the principal and interest of funds borrowed under Article 20, paragraph ②, item 4.
② The management agency may issue Fund bonds at the expense of the Fund following a resolution of the Fund Management Committee. In such cases, Article 156, paragraphs 4 and 5, and Articles 157 through 160 of the Fisheries Cooperatives Act shall apply mutatis mutandis.
③ In addition to matters provided for in paragraph ②, matters necessary for the issuance and offering of Fund bonds and related matters shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Chapter IV Deposit Insurance

Article 28 (Insurance Relationship) The insurance relationship among the management agency, a cooperative, and depositors, etc. shall arise when depositors, etc. acquire claims on deposits, etc. against the cooperative.

Article 29 (Payment of Insurance Premiums)
① A cooperative shall pay insurance premiums for deposits, etc. to the Fund as prescribed by Presidential Decree. The premium rate may differ among cooperatives in consideration of their management and financial condition, the amount of reserves accumulated in each account under Article 26, paragraph ③, and other factors.
② A cooperative that fails to pay insurance premiums by the due date shall pay them to the management agency with the addition of a late payment charge prescribed by Presidential Decree.
③ A cooperative may not request the refund of insurance premiums paid under paragraph ①.
④ Matters necessary for the methods, timing, and other aspects of payment of insurance premiums under paragraph ① shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 29-2 (Establishment of the Target Size of the Fund's Reserves, etc.)
① The management agency shall establish a target size for the Fund's reserves (hereinafter referred to as the “target size” in this Article) so that the reserves remain at an appropriate level.
② The target size shall be determined for each account under Article 26, paragraph ③, following a resolution of the Fund Management Committee, taking into consideration the management and financial condition of cooperatives and other factors, to an extent that does not impair the efficient operation of the mutual finance depositor protection system. The target size may be set as a range with an upper and a lower limit.
③ The management agency shall periodically review the appropriateness of the target size, taking into account the operating conditions of cooperatives, the stability of the mutual finance depositor protection system, and other factors, and may reset the target size if necessary following a resolution of the Fund Management Committee.
④ Notwithstanding Article 29, paragraph ①, when the Fund's reserves reach the target size, the management agency shall reduce or exempt the insurance premiums paid by cooperatives, as prescribed by Presidential Decree, taking into account the amounts of the Fund's anticipated future income and expenditure. In such cases, the management agency shall obtain a resolution of the Fund Management Committee on the decision to reduce or exempt premiums.

Article 30 (Payment of Insurance Proceeds, etc.)
① When an insured event occurs at a cooperative, the management agency shall pay insurance proceeds at the request of the cooperative's depositors, etc., as prescribed by Presidential Decree. However, for a type 1 insured event, the management agency shall decide whether to pay insurance proceeds in accordance with a resolution of the Fund Management Committee within two months of receiving notice under Article 32, paragraph ②.
② In the case of a type 1 insured event, the management agency may, at the request of depositors, etc., pay part of their claims on deposits, etc. in advance, as prescribed by Presidential Decree.
③ The management agency shall publicly announce the commencement date, period, and method of payments under paragraph ① or ② and other necessary matters, as prescribed by Presidential Decree.
④ If a cooperative newly established by a merger or surviving a merger continues the business of a cooperative extinguished by the merger, the newly established cooperative, the surviving cooperative, and the extinguished cooperative shall each be deemed to exist as independent cooperatives for the application of paragraph ① for one year from the date of registration of the merger.
⑤ If a type 2 insured event occurs after a type 1 insured event, the type 2 insured event shall not be treated as an independent insured event for the application of paragraph ①.
⑥ When paying insurance proceeds under paragraph ①, the management agency may withhold payment for up to six months from the insurance payment announcement date under paragraph ③ in respect of amounts prescribed by Presidential Decree, including guarantee obligations owed by depositors, etc. to the cooperative concerned.
⑦ A depositor's right to claim insurance proceeds under paragraph ① shall be extinguished by prescription if not exercised for five years from the commencement date of payments under paragraph ③.

Article 31 (Calculation of Insurance Proceeds, etc.)
① Insurance proceeds payable to each depositor, etc. under Article 30, paragraph ①, shall be the total amount of that depositor's claims on deposits, etc. as of the insurance payment announcement date, less the total amount of debts owed by that depositor to the cooperative concerned, excluding guarantee obligations.
② Insurance proceeds under paragraph ① shall be limited to the amount prescribed by Presidential Decree in consideration of the scale of protected deposits, etc. and other factors.
③ If a depositor, etc. has received an amount in advance under Article 30, paragraph ② (hereinafter referred to as an “advance payment”), the insurance proceeds shall be the amount determined under paragraphs ① and ② less the advance payment.
④ If the advance payment made to a depositor, etc. exceeds the insurance proceeds under paragraphs ① and ②, the depositor, etc. shall return the excess to the management agency. <Amended on February 18, 2020>

Article 32 (Notice of Insured Events, etc.)
① When an insured event occurs, a cooperative shall notify the management agency of that fact without delay.
② The Minister of Oceans and Fisheries shall notify the management agency without delay in any of the following cases. <Amended on March 23, 2013 and February 18, 2020>
1. The Minister has ordered suspension of payment of a cooperative's claims on deposits, etc., or has ordered suspension of business, suspension from duties, or suspension of debt payments under Article 4-2, paragraph ①, item 5, Article 10, paragraph ②, or Articles 170, paragraph 3, and 172, paragraph 3, of the Fisheries Cooperatives Act.
2. The Minister has revoked a cooperative's establishment authorization or approved a resolution for its dissolution.

Article 33 (Acquisition of Claims on Deposits, etc.) The management agency that has paid insurance proceeds and advance payments under Article 30, paragraphs ① and ②, shall acquire the rights of depositors, etc. against the cooperative concerned to the extent of the amounts paid.

Chapter V Supervision, etc.

Article 34 (Supervision)
① The Minister of Oceans and Fisheries shall supervise the business of the management agency and may issue orders necessary for that purpose. <Amended on March 23, 2013>
② If considered necessary for supervision under paragraph ①, the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries may require reports on the business, accounting, property, and other matters of the management agency, or have public officials belonging to the Ministry inspect its business conditions, books, documents, facilities, or other necessary objects. <Amended on March 23, 2013>
③ If considered necessary for supervision under paragraph ①, the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries may request the Governor of the Financial Supervisory Service to inspect the management agency. <Amended on March 23, 2013>

Article 35 (Entrustment of Authority) The Minister of Oceans and Fisheries may entrust part of the Minister's authority under this Act to the chairperson of the Federation or the head of the management agency, as prescribed by Presidential Decree. <Amended on March 23, 2013>

Chapter VI Penalty Provisions <Amended on March 17, 2010>

Article 36 (Criminal Penalties) An officer of a cooperative (excluding a non-standing officer), administrator, or liquidator who fails to carry out the procedures or measures for compliance with an order under Article 4-2, paragraph ①, shall be punished by imprisonment for not more than two years or a criminal fine not exceeding 20 million won. <Amended on February 3, 2015 and February 18, 2020>

Article 37 (Criminal Penalties) Any person falling under either of the following shall be punished by imprisonment for not more than one year or a criminal fine not exceeding 10 million won. <Amended on February 3, 2015>
1. A person who refuses, obstructs, or evades an investigation under Article 18, paragraph ⑦.
2. A person who fails to submit materials or submits false materials in violation of the latter sentence of Article 18, paragraph ⑧.

Article 38 (Joint Penalty Provisions) If an officer, employee, administrator, or liquidator of a cooperative commits a violation under Article 36 or 37 in connection with the cooperative's business, the cooperative shall also be subject to the criminal fine prescribed in the relevant Article, in addition to punishment of the offender. However, this shall not apply if the cooperative has not neglected to exercise reasonable care and supervision over the business concerned to prevent that violation.

Article 39 (Administrative Fines)
① An administrative fine not exceeding 20 million won shall be imposed on a cooperative in any of the following cases:
1. It fails to make the public announcement under Article 11, paragraph ②.
2. It fails to retain or manage materials or make them available for inspection under Article 11, paragraph ⑥.
3. It fails to notify the management agency of the occurrence of an insured event under Article 32, paragraph ①.
② If a cooperative's chairperson, standing director, administrator, or liquidator violates Article 11, paragraph ② or ⑥, an administrative fine not exceeding 10 million won shall be imposed.
③ If a cooperative's chairperson, standing director, or administrator violates Article 32, paragraph ①, an administrative fine not exceeding 2 million won shall be imposed.
④ Administrative fines under paragraphs ① through ③ shall be imposed and collected by the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries, as prescribed by Presidential Decree. <Amended on March 23, 2013>
